Split into outer folds    For each outer fold:    2. Split training into inner folds       For each inner fold:       3. Select features on inner training only       4. Train model    5. text: valid biomarker study, need properly matched cases controls. Using tumor vs. normal tissue organ critical. Important: Never mix normal tissues different organs controls - creates confounding leads inflated performance estimates.
code: # Select pancreatic cancer cases (primary tumors only) pancreatic_cancer <- orginal_TCGA_data[   orginal_TCGA_data$primary_site == "Pancreas" &   orginal_TCGA_data$sample_type == "PrimaryTumor", ]  # Select pancreatic normal controls pancreatic_normal <- orginal_TCGA_data[   orginal_TCGA_data$primary_site == "Pancreas" &   orginal_TCGA_data$sample_type == "SolidTissueNormal", ]  cat("Pancreatic cancer samples:", nrow(pancreatic_cancer), "\n") cat("Pancreatic normal samples:", nrow(pancreatic_normal), "\n")

title: Biomarker Discovery with TCGA Data
text: TCGA often matched normal samples. can carefully add normals related tissues. ⚠️ IMPORTANT WARNING: Adding normal tissues different organs introduces biological confounding. Expression differences organs may dominate tumor vs. normal differences, potentially leading : Inflated performance estimates - may classifying “pancreas vs. colon” rather “tumor vs. normal” Biologically meaningless biomarkers - Features distinguishing tissue types, cancer status Failed external validation - Models trained way often fail tested matched tumor-normal pairs Recommendations: 1. Preferred: Use matched tissue normals, even sample size small 2. Alternative: Use independent normal cohort tissue 3. Last resort: Add related tissue normals, clearly report limitation interpret results extreme caution
code: # If we have fewer than 30 pancreatic normals, add GI tract normals # WARNING: This is a last resort that introduces biological confounding! if (nrow(pancreatic_normal) < 30) {   warning("Adding GI tract normals - this introduces biological confounding!")   message("Adding GI tract normals to increase control sample size")   message("Results should be validated on matched tumor-normal pairs.")    # Add normal tissues from related GI organs   gi_organs <- c("Stomach", "Colon", "Liver and intrahepatic bile ducts")   gi_normals <- orginal_TCGA_data[     orginal_TCGA_data$primary_site %in% gi_organs &     orginal_TCGA_data$sample_type == "SolidTissueNormal",   ]    # Sample to avoid overwhelming imbalance   set.seed(42)   n_to_add <- min(50, nrow(gi_normals))   gi_sample <- gi_normals[sample(nrow(gi_normals), n_to_add), ]    pancreatic_normal <- rbind(pancreatic_normal, gi_sample)   cat("Total controls after augmentation:", nrow(pancreatic_normal), "\n")   cat("WARNING: These results may be confounded by tissue-type differences.\n") }

OmicSelector 2.0 prioritizes **zero data leakage** **feature stability** raw accuracy metrics. High accuracy unstable feature sets ("Rashomon Effect") indicates overfitting, real signal. ## Migration v1.0 Legacy functions like `OmicSelector_iteratedRFE` deprecated due data leakage issues. title: Nogueira Stability Index for Feature Selection — stability
text: Nogueira Stability Index preferred Jaccard/Kuncheva indices invariant number selected features. high stability (close 1) indicates features consistently selected across different training subsets, suggesting robust signal rather overfitting specific data splits. Formula: $$S = 1 - \frac{V}{V_0}$$ : - V = (1/p) * sum(pi_j * (1 - pi_j)) [observed variance] - V_0 = (k_bar/p) * (1 - k_bar/p) [expected variance random selection] - pi_j = selection frequency feature j - k_bar = average number selected features - p = total number candidate features
